title: Isandro and the Room
premise: Isandro Vey, a night-shift pest controller in the drowned town of Hollowmere, is hired to clear a house where something leaves fingerprints in the dust — prints too large, and always facing the door. The house belongs to Ada Joubert, who has recorded her own sleep for seven years to prove the noises have explanations; the recordings now capture a second voice answering questions she never asked aloud. As Isandro investigates, he learns the entity was invited in decades ago by Ada's father as a bargain for the family's survival, and it has come to collect the last Joubert. Holding out until sunrise, Isandro must choose between his duty to report what he's found and his growing love for Ada — and in the end he takes the invitation into himself, letting the frost claim him in her place, so that justice is done outside any law and the house finally goes quiet.
about_author: Freya Dunmore is a former building inspector from the coastal fens who spent years documenting condemned houses before turning to horror. She writes in unheated rooms, on the theory that fear should be researched, not imagined.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Isandro, a weary pest controller working nights to outrun his debts, takes a last-minute job at 14 Marrow Lane. The house is warm despite the frost outside, and the dust shows a single line of enormous footprints ending at the front door. His POV establishes dread and routine; the beat is the first crack in his skepticism.

chapters.title: Fingerprints in the Flour
chapters.summary: Isandro inspects the kitchen and finds five-fingered prints pressed into spilled flour — human in shape, wrong in proportion. Ada Joubert watches him from the stairs, unsurprised. His POV; the emotional beat is the humiliation of a professional confronting evidence his training cannot explain.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Tapes
chapters.summary: Ada shows Isandro her wall of sleep recordings, one cassette per night for seven years, kept to prove the noises are rats, pipes, settling wood. She plays a tape of her own snoring — and a low voice beneath it. Alternating POV begins; the beat is complicit fear shared between strangers.

chapters.title: Questions She Never Asked
chapters.summary: On tape, the voice answers things: 'Not yet,' it says, when no question was voiced. Ada admits she stopped listening years ago. Isandro's POV; the beat is the horror of realizing the entity has been patient, and patience is worse than violence.

chapters.title: The Contract of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Isandro searches the town records office and finds Ada's father's name in a 1987 petition — fourteen households that 'invited in' something to survive the floods. Twelve houses burned; two remain. His POV; the beat is dread turning into purpose.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Elderly Mr. Sallow, the other surviving household's owner, tells Isandro the bargain's terms: the thing protects its invited houses from everything except itself, and it takes the last of each bloodline. Ada's POV; the beat is grief for a father she defended all her life.

chapters.title: What the Frost Writes
chapters.summary: Fern-frost patterns bloom on Ada's windows in shapes too deliberate — a hand, a doorway, a countdown. Isandro photographs them; by morning the photos show only blank glass. His POV; the beat is the erosion of any safe, observable reality.

chapters.title: Night Two
chapters.summary: Isandro stays the night in the house, professional pride and something warmer keeping him there. At 3:11 a.m. the second voice says his name, correctly, though he never gave it. His POV; the beat is the collapse of anonymity as protection.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: In the attic, Isandro finds Ada's father's ledger: dates, payments of hair and blood, and one line circled — 'the last one pays for all.' He hides it from Ada. His POV; the beat is the first lie between them, love already complicating honesty.

chapters.title: Ada's Dreaming Voice
chapters.summary: Isandro records Ada sleeping; she speaks in the second voice's cadence, answering its questions in her father's phrases. She wakes with frost on her lips. Ada's POV; the beat is terror at becoming the entity's instrument.

chapters.title: Sallow's Warning
chapters.summary: Sallow begs Isandro to take Ada out of Hollowmere before the frost finishes — the thing cannot cross running water or the town boundary. But Ada refuses to run; she wants to face what her father invited. Ada's POV; the beat is love against duty, stated plainly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Thing About Explanations
chapters.summary: Isandro tries every rational tool — thermal cameras, humidity readings — and the readings all point to one conclusion: the cold is coming from inside the walls, breathing. His POV; the beat is the scientist's surrender, strangely a relief.

chapters.title: A Night Off
chapters.summary: A quiet chapter: Isandro and Ada cook dinner, laugh at old tapes, and admit they've been alone in the same loneliness for years. The frost waits politely at the windows. Alternating POV; the beat is tenderness that makes the coming loss unbearable.

chapters.title: The Second House
chapters.summary: They visit Sallow's home and find it empty, frost fern covering every surface in the exact pattern of Ada's windows. Sallow is gone — taken early, out of order. Isandro's POV; the beat is the rules changing, the countdown accelerating.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: Ada finally reads her father's full ledger and learns the truth: he invited the thing to save her infant life during the floods, trading her eventual debt for her childhood. Ada's POV; the beat is fury, then a terrible tenderness toward a dead man's desperate love.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Signed
chapters.summary: A defrocked priest, one of the fourteen petitioners' descendants, confirms the rite: an invitation must be freely renewed to be collected, and the thing will manufacture consent if denied. His POV cameo through Isandro's interview; the beat is learning the trap has a legal shape.

chapters.title: Consent, Manufactured
chapters.summary: Ada begins dreaming invitations — her father's voice asking her to 'let him finish the work.' She wakes with her hand on the front door latch. Isandro's POV; the beat is the horror of a mind being slowly argued with.

chapters.title: Barricade
chapters.summary: Isandro seals the house: salt lines, running taps, recorded bells on loop. The voice laughs through the speakers — it has heard all of this before, in twelve burned houses. His POV; the beat is defiance curdling into futility.

chapters.title: The Frost Advances
chapters.summary: Ice creeps inward from the walls, fern by fern, each pattern a word in a language Ada's sleeping mouth translates. The message: 'Three nights.' Alternating POV; the beat is a deadline made physical.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: They flee toward the river with the town boundary in sight; the cold follows in the ditches, freezing the water solid ahead of them, building a road of ice. Ada's POV; the beat is the rules bending — the thing is allowed to make its own path to what it's owed.

chapters.title: The Boundary
chapters.summary: At the town line the frost stops, and for one day Ada is free, warm, almost laughing in a motel outside Hollowmere. Isandro watches her sleep without the voice. His POV; the beat is false peace, the eye of the storm.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Phone
chapters.summary: The motel phone rings at 3:11. The voice doesn't threaten — it negotiates, offering to take Isandro instead, 'a volunteer, freely given.' He hangs up and lies to Ada about the call. His POV; the beat is the temptation of sacrifice, kept secret.

chapters.title: Why He Says Yes
chapters.summary: In flashback, Isandro's history: a brother he failed to protect, a lifetime of debts paid to the wrong people. Taking Ada's place would be the first just thing he's ever done. His POV; the beat is motive laid bare — justice outside the law, love against duty.

chapters.title: Ada Finds Out
chapters.summary: Ada discovers the ledger Isandro hid, with his handwriting added: a renewal of the invitation, himself as signatory. She confronts him with the frost already forming on the motel glass. Ada's POV; the beat is rage at being protected without consent.

chapters.title: The Argument at the Edge
chapters.summary: They fight at the frozen river — she won't let him pay her father's debt, he won't let her pay it. The ice road to Hollowmere glitters behind them, patient. Alternating POV; the beat is love weaponized as an obstacle, each trying to out-die the other.

chapters.title: The Third Night
chapters.summary: They return together, having agreed on a third option: neither signs, and they hold the house until sunrise, when the collection window closes. The frost begins writing its final pattern on every window at once. His POV; the beat is grim resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: The entity stops being subtle: doors open onto the inside of the walls, the voice speaks in Sallow's newly dead timbre, the temperature drops toward killing cold. They burn furniture to stay alive. Ada's POV; the beat is endurance as an act of love.

chapters.title: What It Shows Them
chapters.summary: The thing offers visions: Isandro's brother alive in the frost, Ada's father apologizing, the twelve burned households whole again. Each vision asks, gently, for one signature. Alternating POV; the beat is temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: Isandro Almost Signs
chapters.summary: Alone by the dying fire, pen in hand, Isandro hears his brother say 'you always were the slow one.' He burns the ledger page instead. His POV; the beat is the hardest no, grief finally answered honestly.

chapters.title: Ada's Answer
chapters.summary: The entity shifts tactics and asks Ada the one question she can't refuse: whether she forgives her father. Her sleeping voice says yes — and the frost reads it as renewal. Ada's POV; the beat is the trap sprung through love itself.

chapters.title: The Door in the Frost
chapters.summary: A door of ice opens in the hallway, and through it: the floods of 1987, the fourteen households kneeling, her father's wet handprint on a contract of frost. The collection begins. His POV; the beat is the past made present and inescapable.

chapters.title: Sunrise Is Not Enough
chapters.summary: Dawn comes — and the frost doesn't stop. The priest's information was incomplete: sunrise closes the window only for the invited bloodline. A volunteer's window stays open. Isandro understands what he must do. His POV; the beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Renewal
chapters.summary: Isandro speaks the invitation freely, in his own words, taking the debt of the Joubert line onto himself. The frost turns from Ada's windows to his. Ada's POV; the beat is heartbreak and awe — love against duty resolved by choosing both.

chapters.title: Ada Refuses the Gift
chapters.summary: Ada fights the collection itself: she re-reads the original contract aloud and finds the flaw her father never saw — a debt freely assumed can be freely discharged, by anyone who loves the debtor enough to claim it. She begins the counter-rite. Ada's POV; the beat is justice outside the law, found in the fine print.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern
chapters.summary: The frost writes its last design across the whole house — not a countdown now but a scale, weighing Isandro's offered life against the original debt. The house groans, deciding. His POV; the beat is suspended judgment, the longest minute of the book.

chapters.title: Sunrise, Second Attempt
chapters.summary: As the sun clears the ridge, Ada completes the discharge: she forgives the debt out loud, names it paid, and the frost — bound by its own contract's language — must honor it. The ice door shatters. Alternating POV; the beat is the climax's release, victory by word rather than force.

chapters.title: What the House Keeps
chapters.summary: The entity withdraws, but not wholly: it leaves one frost fern on the kitchen window, shaped like a handshake — the bargain honored, the invitation still technically open, forever. Isandro and Ada choose to keep the house anyway. His POV; the beat is uneasy peace.

chapters.title: The Recordings End
chapters.summary: Ada records one final night: silence, then her own voice saying goodnight to the house. She gives the seven years of tapes to the priest's archive so no other family signs blind. Ada's POV; the beat is turning survival into testimony.

chapters.title: Two Survivors
chapters.summary: Spring comes to Hollowmere. Isandro quits pest control; Ada repaints the kitchen over the flour prints, leaving one, framed. They are not unmarked — the cold still finds them on some nights — but they face it together. Alternating POV; the beat is love that outlasted the debt.

chapters.title: The Last Frost
chapters.summary: A coda: years later, a new family moves into Sallow's old house and finds a ledger in the attic. Across town, Ada and Isandro read the frost on their window — a single word, 'remember' — and drive through the night to answer the call. His POV, closing the loop; the beat is vigilance as devotion, the story ending where duty begins again.
